text: In a circle, equal straight-lines are equally far from the center, and (straight-lines) which are equally far from the center are equal to one another. Let $ABDC$$^{\,\dag}$ be a circle, and let $AB$ and $CD$ be equal straight-lines within it. I say that $AB$ and $CD$ are equally far from the center.
For let the center of circle $ABDC$ be found [Prop.~3.1], and let it be (at) $E$.
And let $EF$ and $EG$ be drawn from (point) $E$, perpendicular to $AB$ and $CD$ (respectively) [Prop.~1.12].
And let $AE$ and $EC$ be joined.
Therefore, since some straight-line, $EF$, through the center (of the circle), cuts some (other) straight-line, $AB$, not through the center, at right-angles, it also cuts it in half [Prop.~3.3].
assertion: EF bisects AB (cuts AB in half)

spans.text: some straight-line, $EF$, through the center (of the circle), cuts some (other) straight-line, $AB$, not through the center, at right-angles

spans.label: assertion

text: Thus, the (sum of the squares) on $AF$ and $FE$ is equal to the (sum of the squares) on $CG$ and $GE$, of which the (square) on $AF$ is equal to the (square) on $CG$. For $AF$ is equal to $CG$.
assertion: sum of squares on AF and FE equals sum of squares on CG and GE, with AF² = CG²

text: Thus, $EF$ (is) equal to $EG$.
assertion: EF equals EG

text: And straight-lines in a circle are said to be equally far from the center when perpendicular (straight-lines) which are drawn to them from the center are equal [Def.~3.4]. Thus, $AB$ and $CD$ are equally far from the center.
assertion: AB and CD are equally far from the center

text: Thus, in a circle, equal straight-lines are equally far from the center, and (straight-lines) which are equally far from the center are equal to one another. (Which is) the very thing it was required to show.
